payload.court: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal( Pilot Court) Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
payload.holding: The tribunal held that the claimants in both petitions are entitled to compensation for death and injuries caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, payable by the insurance company.
payload.ratio: In motor accident claim petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the claimants must establish the occurrence on the touchstone of preponderance of probability, and criminal records such as an FIR and chargesheet are sufficient prima facie proof of negligence when unrebutted.

payload.holding: The tribunal held that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending truck by Respondent No. 1, and awarded compensation across the four connected claim petitions to be paid by the insurance company.

payload.holding: The Tribunal held the insurance company liable to pay compensation to the three injured claimants after deducting 50% for contributory negligence due to driving without a license and helmets.
payload.ratio: In motor accident claim cases under Section 166 of the MV Act, the standard of proof is based on preponderance of probabilities, and police record documents such as the FIR and charge sheet are sufficient to establish negligence in the absence of rebuttal. Furthermore, contributory negligence is established when the injured rider is proven to have been driving without a valid driving license and without wearing a helmet.

Tribunal can be initiated either on an application for compensation made by the
persons aggrieved (the claimants) under Section 166(1) or Section 163-A of the Act or

proceedings are suo motu initiated by the Tribunal.

respondents. The insurer is not a respondent, but a notice under Section 149(2) of the
Act. Where a claim petition is filed by the injured or by the legal representatives of a
person dying in a motor accident, the driver and owner have to be impleaded as
respondents. The claimants need not implead the insurer as a party. But they have
the choice of impleading the insurer also as a party-respondent. When it is not

payload.holding: The court held that a legal representative who was not dependent upon the deceased at the time of death is not entitled to compensation under the head 'loss of dependency', reducing the total compensation accordingly.

Motor Vehicle against third party risk. Driving an uninsured vehicle is an offence punishable with an
imprisonment extending up to three months or the fine which may extend to Rs. 1,000 or both; (2)
